Schedule a 2-hour private deployment workshop (network & PKI) the week of 2025-06-09

meeting_header:
Date: 2025-05-29
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE - 2nd half), Maya Chen (KelpTech Head of ML), Liam O'Connor (KelpTech CTO), Sofia Alvarez (KelpTech SRE), Diego Ramos (Product)
summary: Quick scoping call to align POC success criteria and decide deployment mode (hosted vs dedicated vs private). Primary goals: define workload sizing (RPS / concurrency / token mix), measurable success criteria (latency P95, correctness/regression thresholds, cost band), benchmark plan and timeline for a 4-6 week pilot. Security & data residency are gating items for Private. Action: Redwood to send benchmark template and hosted cost/throughput estimates; KelpTech to share traces and finalize timeline.
topics:
1) Success criteria: latency (P95) target, quality regressions, cost per 1M tokens
2) Workload sizing: QPS, concurrency, average tokens per request, burst patterns
3) Benchmarks: synthetic vs replay, perf metrics, KV cache/prefix considerations
4) Deployment decision factors: data residency, SLA, throughput predictability, egress and network constraints
5) Timeline & owners: 4-6 week pilot, deliverables and checkpoints
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Great, thanks everyone for joining, we'll keep this tight, about 45-ish minutes, goal is to lock success criteria and decide which mode we should pilot, hosted, dedicated or private.
[00:19] Maya Chen: Yeah thanks, quick context — we've got prod traffic patterns from a beta chat assistant, roughly 120 RPS average during peaks, bursts to 350 for short windows, avg tokens per request around 280-340 depending on prompt.
[00:38] Priya Nair (Redwood): Got it. When you say 120 RPS is that sustained or 120 concurrent requests?
[00:44] Maya Chen: That's requests per second, sustained over 10-15 minute windows. Concurrency is usually about 60 at that RPS.
[00:53] Liam O'Connor: Important piece — we need P95 under 200ms for user-facing retrieval + generate flows, else product folks will push back.
[01:03] Jordan Lee: Okay P95 < 200ms is a helpful SLO. For cost, do you have a target? Some internal target like sub-$50 per 1M tokens?
[01:12] Diego Ramos: We're aiming for sub-$40 ideally, but we know with larger models we might trade some cost for quality.
[01:20] Priya Nair: Noted. A couple of clarifying Qs — what's the data sensitivity for the prompts? Any PHI?
[01:26] Maya Chen: No PHI in current dataset, but there are customer emails and proprietary product specs, so encryption at rest, audit logs and SOC2-ish controls are required.
[01:36] Sofia Alvarez: And residency — we need EU-only hosting for a subset of traffic and the option for on-prem later for compliance audits.
[01:44] Jordan Lee: That pushes Private or Dedicated with region pinning as important considerations. Hosted can do region routing but if you need on-prem later, Redwood Private path is designed for that.
[01:55] Liam O'Connor: How often do we see regressions when model versions roll? We want guardrails.
[02:00] Priya Nair: We recommend a canary + automatic fallback policy. Also our Optimize tooling will surface quality regressions tied to prompt sets — we can include that in the pilot.
[02:10] Maya Chen: For benchmarks, we can provide a replay of 7 days. Will that be sufficient?
[02:16] Priya Nair: Yes — a 7-day traces with token counts gives us the burn-rate and burst profile. We'll run both replay and synthetic worst-case runs.
[02:24] Jordan Lee: On the hosted vs dedicated question: hosted is fastest to start and cheapest for low steady-state. Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools and more predictable throughput at scale. Private gives full network control and auditability but higher setup.
[02:39] Diego Ramos: Curious about autoscaling — for dedicated, can you still autoscale for bursts or is that a manual reserve?
[02:45] Priya Nair: You get configurable autoscaling and optional burst capacity — it's policy driven. There's a tradeoff: larger reserve reduces risk of cold capacity failure but costs more.
[02:55] Marco Ruiz: If I jump in — with your tokens and RPS, initial estimation shows hosted can cover baseline but your peak bursts push into a dedicated-reserved footprint unless you accept degraded latency during bursts or fallback to a cheaper model variant.
[03:08] Maya Chen: Model variants meaning smaller quantized models? We need quality checks against our golden prompt set.
[03:14] Priya Nair: Exactly — we can fallback to a quantized variant with similar outputs, but we'd run evals to ensure quality delta is acceptable. Our Optimize recommendations will include quantization profiles per workload.
[03:25] Sofia Alvarez: Networking — if we go Private, we need KMS integration and our HSM for key wrapping. Is that supported?
[03:31] Jordan Lee: Yes, Private supports KMS/HSM integration and customer-managed keys; we log key usage in audit logs.
[03:37] Liam O'Connor: What's the expected timeline to get an on-prem or VPC private instance up?
[03:42] Priya Nair: Typical Private on-prem takes 6-8 weeks (network, firewall, PKI, infra validation) — VPC-hosted Private can be shorter, 3-4 weeks depending on approvals. Hosted and Dedicated pilots can start in 1-2 weeks for a hosted POC.
[03:56] Maya Chen: OK so for MVP we probably want Hosted pilot first to validate quality & cost, then Dedicated reserve if we need throughput, and keep Private as the compliance path.
[04:06] Jordan Lee: That aligns with what we see. Proposed success criteria for the POC: 1) Replay 7-day trace with P95 <= 200ms for customer-facing flows on the chosen model; 2) Quality regressions <= 5% on golden prompt set vs baseline; 3) Cost estimate within the target band (sub-$40-$50 per 1M tokens); 4) Audit log and encryption proof-of-concept for sample requests.
[04:34] Diego Ramos: Sounds good. Can you clarify what metrics you'll provide in the benchmark report?
[04:39] Priya Nair: We'll provide P50/P95/P99 latencies, tokens/sec throughput, GPU utilization, cost per 1M tokens, and regression heatmaps for your prompt set. We'll also include KV-cache hit rates if we enable prefix caching during the replay.
[04:55] Maya Chen: About KV cash — we saw notes in the docs about prefix cache, will that need app changes?
[04:59] Marco Ruiz: Small SDK change for explicit prefixes in some cases; in many cases we can do automatic prefix caching based on request patterns, but we'll confirm in the benchmark run.
[05:09] Sofia Alvarez: Security doc ask — can you send SOC2 audit section and network requirements?
[05:13] Jordan Lee: Yes, we'll attach the security packet. We'll also include a checklist for on-prem firewall/NAT rules.
[05:20] Liam O'Connor: For decision criteria, I'd like a short rubric: if 99th latency under hosted meets SLO and cost okay, go hosted. If latency unpredictable or bursts cause >20% error/latency degradation, go dedicated. If data residency or audits require physical separation, choose Private.
[05:37] Jordan Lee: Perfect — we'll draft that rubric and include in the follow-up.
[05:42] Diego Ramos: Any notes on benchmarking infra — do you need GPU types?
[05:46] Priya Nair: Yes, tell us preferred instance families if you have restrictions; otherwise we will test on our standard T4/P100 equivalents and report model-by-hardware profiles.
[05:56] Maya Chen: We prefer A100 if possible for parity with our training, but we understand cost tradeoffs.
[06:02] Jordan Lee: Noted. Action recap...
[06:06] [crosstalk]
[06:08] Jordan Lee: Jordan to send template and pricing, Maya to upload traces, Priya to run hosted sim — aim to have initial benchmark results in ~10 business days.
[06:17] Maya Chen: Works for us.
[06:18] Jordan Lee: Anything else?
[06:20] Sofia Alvarez: Quick ask — can the security packet include a network diagram sample for Private?
[06:25] Jordan Lee: Yes, we'll include a sample architecture.
[06:28] Liam O'Connor: Thanks all.
[06:30] Jordan Lee: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with next steps and link to the benchmark spreadsheet.
[06:35] [recording ends]
